chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from some of our companions from Aban from Aamir ibn Juza'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who has a sale (item) and sets a known fixed price: whoever remains silent from him among those who buy from him, he sells it to him at that price; and whoever bargains with him and refuses to buy from him at that price, he increases the price for him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he increases it for two men or three, there is no problem with that. But as for him doing it with every one who refuses to him and bargains with him, and prevents it from those who did not do that, then I do not like it except that he sells it with one price (for everyone).'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on variable pricing and bargaining in trade according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of fairness in market transactions, specifically addressing the practice of variable pricing based on a buyer's willingness to negotiate. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiques the arbitrary nature of raising prices only for those who haggle, advocating instead for a uniform price to ensure equity and prevent exploitation. This reflects the broader Shia ethical emphasis on transparency and consistency in commercial dealings as a form of social justice.
